newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PEKAO TO CONTROL BANKING GROUP IN OCTOBER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PEKAO TO CONTROL BANKING GROUP IN OCTOBER.

text.p: Poland's Bank Pekao SA, heading a a group of state-owned banks which are soon to be consolidated, will receive 100 percent stakes of the other three banks in the scheme in October at latest, a deputy finance minister said.
"Under the plan, 100 percent of the shares would be transferred to the group leader no later than October," Ryszard Pazura told a news conference on Wednesday.

On Wednesday Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA (PBG), Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA (BDK) and Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA (PBKS) agreed to the final shape of an agreement which groups them under the Warsaw-based Pekao SA.

The nominal value of the three state-owned banks was about 100 million zlotys, but their owned funds and market value were much larger, said Pekao deputy president Andrzej Dorosz, also present at the conference.

"The share capital of the three banks is relatively small compared to their owned funds and potential market value," Pekao's Dorosz said of the banking group which will control about 20 percent Poland's banking service sector.

The finance ministry said that Pekao will receive the shares after shareholders of each of the three banks, as well as the Anti-Monopoly Office and the National Bank of Poland give the final go-ahead.
Under the plan, Pekao SA would be privatised following the end of the consolidation process, designed to strengthen the banking sector to face international competition.
